title: Convoy throttle and inflight-quarantine for multi-region active-active failover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a convoy-throttle pattern with an inflight-quarantine mechanism to reduce tail amplification during active-active multi-region failovers for the hosted API gateway. This ticket covers behavioral contract, the rate-controller algorithm, streaming session lease reconciliation, circuit breakers integration, and the rollout plan. Goal: keep user-visible P99 latency and error rate within SLOs during region degradations while minimizing dropped tokens for streaming sessions.
goals: Prevent amplification (request storms) when a region becomes degraded by applying a coordinated, telemetry-driven throttle ("convoy throttle") at the ingress gateways
Preserve in-flight streaming sessions where possible by quarantining and reconciling leases instead of blindly dropping sockets
Integrate with existing circuit breaker subsystem so per-route/tenant circuits prevent cascading failures
Provide clear observability: dashboards, SLO alerts, and post-mortem signals to measure success
Rollout incrementally with canaries and an automated rollback if error budgets spike
acceptance_criteria: During simulated single-region degradation, P95 and P99 latency remain within the configured SLO for 90% of test runs
In streaming cutover tests, >=75% of sessions can resume without token loss after failover when quarantine is enabled
Dashboard surfaces convoy-throttle state, per-tenant throttle fractional allocation, and circuit trips
Automated policy toggles (canary -> global) work and tied alerts trigger rollback when error budget > threshold
Documentation and runbook added to Console runbooks with steps for manual override
design_decisions: Place convoy-throttle at the regional gateway ingress layer so decisions are local and fast; use a central policy controller only for configuration and gradual rollout
Throttle is proportional and occupancy-aware: each tenant receives a fraction of spare capacity rather than a flat RPS cap to avoid starving high-SLO customers
Quarantine model: convert streaming sockets to a lightweight 'lease' state with metadata (kv-lease id) and keep KV-cache-based continuations in-flight for a bounded window (configurable: default 30s)
Circuit breakers remain the last resort: queues and throttle should exhaust first before per-route circuits trip; circuits are driven by error budgets and request saturation signals
Telemetry gating: use a rolling-window headroom metric derived from regional tail latency and GPU backlog to begin gradual traffic egress rather than an all-or-nothing shift
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype convoy-throttle controller (local algorithm) with a feature flag in the edge gateway
2) Implement lease conversion and lightweight quarantine path for streaming sockets with a TTL and resume token persisted to KV
3) Wire throttle decisions into the existing circuit breaker API (trip thresholds and soft trips)
4) Add per-tenant allocation policy and configuration knobs in Console and API (weights, minimum reserved, emergency floor)
5) Add observability: Prometheus metrics, histograms for throttle ratio, lease-resume success, and synthetic SLO probes
6) Run canary experiments in a single pair of regions, execute chaos tests and load tests, iterate on thresholds
7) Global rollout with staged exposure and automated rollback hooks tied to SLO alerting

blockers: Need a KV-perf budget approval for storing short-lived lease records at target QPS
Security review for the new lease metadata persisted across regions (customer-specific PII checks)
Dependence on infra team's rollout window for the gateway feature flagging layer
risks: Incorrect throttle weights could starve low-volume high-SLO tenants — mitigation: emergency floor and canary with targeted tenants
Lease persistence overhead under large fanout can increase KV costs — mitigation: TTL enforcement and compaction policy
Edge code complexity increases failure modes for long-lived streaming sockets — mitigation: comprehensive chaos tests and fallback to immediate close when reconciliation fails
testing_plan: Unit tests for throttle decision logic and per-tenant allocator
End-to-end simulation: fault-inject region degradation and verify throttle gating and session resume rates
Chaos test: flip central policy controller and validate local ingress maintains safe behavior
SRE runbook dry-run: simulate manual rollback and validate alert triggers and SLA impact notifications
observability_and_alerting: Metrics: region_spare_capacity_ratio, convoy_throttle_fraction{tenant}, lease_resume_success_ratio, circuit_soft_trips, throttle_rollout_stage
Dashboards: multi-region failover overview with per-tenant SLO burn rate overlay
Alerts: SLO burn > 2x for 5m (auto rollback), lease_resume_success_ratio < 0.6 for 10m
Runbook: steps to manually toggle convoy-throttle, quarantine TTL, and initiate rollback

notes: This ticket intentionally biases toward preserving user streaming progress over strict immediate fail-open behavior; tradeoff chosen to reduce user-visible token loss at the cost of short-lived KV statefulness
We expect post-rollout telemetry to surface tenant-level anomalies; plan to iterate allocation heuristics based on real traffic patterns
